messages:
maria_devex: Quick note — the Next.js edge sample in the JS quickstart breaks for me when run on Vercel's Edge runtime. Error: "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module". I was following the example that uses require(). Anyone else hit this?

jonathan_sdk: Hmm yeah that sounds like a CJS/ESM mismatch. Edge runtimes are ESM-only so require() will fail. The SDK originally had both entrypoints but our quickstart might be showing the CJS snippet by accident. Can you paste the exact snippet and the file path?

maria_devex: It's the example under examples/nextjs-edge/api/generate.ts — the snippet in the docs shows:
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
```
and the runtime blows up at deploy. Local node (server mode) worked, but edge fails.

lee_runtime: Confirmed — edge runtimes (V8 isolates, edge functions) require ESM. Also typescript -> emit can produce CJS if tsconfig not set. Two quick fixes: switch to ESM imports or use dynamic import inside the handler. Example ESM (preferred):
```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
export default async function handler(req) { /* ... */ }
```
Or dynamic import inside the function if you need to keep a CJS consumer:
```ts
export default async function handler(req) {
  const { createClient } = await import('@redwood/inference');
  const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
}
```
Both avoid the static require problem. Also note if you're using TypeScript, set "module": "esnext" and "moduleResolution": "node16" (or nodeNext) to preserve ESM output.

katie_docs: Thanks — we accidentally shipped the CJS example in the edge quickstart. We'll update docs to show both ESM and a dynamic-import fallback with a clear callout about edge runtimes + TS config. Can you confirm if the SDK export shape is named only (createClient) or default too? That affects the snippet.

jonathan_sdk: Current published package provides both named exports and a default export for convenience, but default export is CJS-friendly and can confuse TS consumers regarding types if esModuleInterop is off. Recommend docs show the named import for TS examples (better types), and a small note: if you rely on require(), do dynamic import in edge or use the CJS entry in node servers.

maria_devex: Also ran into a typing oddity — with `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` my IDE resolved a generic `any` for the default and autocomplete was meh. With `import { createClient }` types are solid. Might be worth surfacing that in the SDK README.

lee_runtime: That matches what we've seen — default export gets wrapped and loses some type inference without esModuleInterop: true or allowSyntheticDefaultImports. Docs should call this out and show both options.

ci-bot: Build #4821 failed on branch docs/edge-import-fix: examples/nextjs-edge integration test errored (Edge deploy). See https://ci.internal/redwood/4821

katie_docs: Got it. I'll open a docs PR to: 1) replace require() with named ESM import in the edge quickstart, 2) add a small TS troubleshooting section about tsconfig + esModuleInterop, 3) include a dynamic import pattern for readers needing compatibility. Will link PR here.

jonathan_sdk: One more compatibility note to include: if folks are bundling (webpack/next), ensure the bundler target is set to 'esnext' for edge / set experiments.outputModule for older setups — otherwise bundlers may rewrite imports into CJS form.

maria_devex: awesome, thanks. If you tag me on the PR I'll test the updated example on our Vercel preview.

katie_docs: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/345 — will include the snippets + short explanation about named vs default and recommended TS settings.

jonathan_sdk: Great. After PR merges we should add a short blurb to the SDK changelog and maybe a small note in the quickstart CI that runs the example in an edge-like runner to catch regressions.

maria_devex: Sounds perfect. :thumbsup:
